key_insight: AI-assisted simulations reveal how SrTiO₃ grain-boundary composition and atomic reconstruction control electronic states, electric fields, and local polarization.
engineering_relevance: These findings could guide oxide-perovskite interface engineering to control carrier localization and band alignment, but solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Combine Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential to search boundary structures and compositions.
Map chemical-potential stability and compare structural motifs across three grain-boundary geometries.
Use density functional theory and electrostatic analysis to characterize electronic states, fields, and polarization.
evidence_signal: For Σ5(310)[001] boundaries, the calculations identify ten stable structures in four motif families and four electronic regimes: localized electron-doped, delocalized electron-doped, insulating, and hole-attracting.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational predictions rather than experimental validation; transfer to photovoltaic materials and devices remains untested.
paper_title: Uncovering the Structural, Electronic, and Electrostatic Landscapes of SrTiO$_3$ Grain Boundaries via Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
